changes.before: Create the labeled note textarea with four visible rows, an eighty-unit limit and the supplied initial text between its tags.
changes.after: Make a text box that can hold several lines.

before: textarea provides a multiline text control. Unlike an input’s value attribute, its initial text goes between opening and closing tags. A label remains necessary; existing text is not a substitute for the field name.

rows="4" requests a visible height measured in text lines, not a four-line submission limit. maxlength="80" sets a text-length limit measured in UTF-16 code units; one visible character can occupy more than one unit. name="note" supplies the submitted key. This example is optional because required is absent.

```html
<form>
  <label for="note">Observation</label>
  <textarea id="note" name="note" rows="4" maxlength="80">Saw two moths.</textarea>
  <button type="submit">Send observation</button>
</form>
```
The initial field text is Saw two moths. A value="Other text" attribute on textarea would not supply its initial value. Users can edit the content; the original text in markup is the default, not a live copy of later edits. Browser user-entry limits and scripted changes have different constraint-validation rules, so do not infer typing behavior from an attribute check.

Create the labeled note textarea with four visible rows, an eighty-unit limit and the supplied initial text between its tags. The supplied checks inspect markup or local form-data relationships; they do not submit a network request or certify a screen-reader or native-browser experience. Optional local practice: try the changed case in a disposable local page and explain the difference.
after: `<textarea>` is a field for several lines of text. Put its starting text between the opening and closing tags. Give it a label so the person knows what to write.

`rows="4"` asks for a box about four text lines tall. It does not limit the answer to four lines. `maxlength="80"` limits the length of a typed answer. It counts text units: ordinary English letters use one each, but some symbols, such as emoji, use more.

This field starts with a short observation.

```html
<form>
  <label for="note">Observation</label>
  <textarea id="note" name="note" rows="4" maxlength="80">Saw two moths.</textarea>
  <button type="submit">Send observation</button>
</form>
```

The label points to `id="note"`. `name="note"` names the sent value. `rows` sets the height and `maxlength` sets the text limit. `Saw two moths.` is inside the tags, so it is the starting text.

Add the shown field inside main. Use id and name `note`, four rows, and maxlength `80`. Put exactly `Saw two moths.` between its tags. Do not use a `value` attribute for the starting text. Add its label, then run the checks.

before.question: Change only rows from 4 to 8. Has the maxlength limit doubled?
choices: The initial text becomes eight empty lines.
Yes, rows multiplies the character limit.
No. The requested visible height changes; maxlength remains 80.
before.explanation: rows and maxlength have separate jobs. Neither changing height nor retaining default text rewrites the length attribute.

after.question: You change rows from 4 to 8. Does that double the text limit?
choices: It replaces the starting text with blank lines.
Yes, the box can now store twice as much.
No. The box is taller, but maxlength stays 80.
after.explanation: Height and text length are separate settings.
